import torch

# Define the custom CUDA kernel for matrix multiplication (A.T @ B)
# We implement a tiled matrix multiplication using shared memory and thread blocks.
# This is a simplified version of the classic GEMM kernel.

elementwise_add_source = """
#include <torch/extension.h>
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

__global__ void elementwise_add_kernel(const float* a, const float* b, float* out, int size) {
    int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (idx < size) {
        out[idx] = a[idx] + b[idx];
    }
}

torch::Tensor elementwise_add_cuda(torch::Tensor a, torch::Tensor b) {
    auto size = a.numel();
    auto out = torch::zeros_like(a);

    const int block_size = 256;
    const int num_blocks = (size + block_size - 1) / block_size;

    elementwise_add_kernel<<<num_blocks, block_size>>>(a.data_ptr<float>(), b.data_ptr<float>(), out.data_ptr<float>(), size);

    return out;
}
"""

Let me design:

- Define a kernel `matmul_kernel` that takes pointers to A, B, C, and dimensions M, K, N. It launches enough threads (total threads = M * N). Each thread computes one element C[row][col] = sum_{k=0}^{K-1} A[k][row] * B[k][col].

But we need to map threadIdx.x and threadIdx.y appropriately. Suppose we use a 1D grid with blockSize = 256. Then each thread gets an index `idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x`. We can compute row = idx / N, col = idx % N. Because there are N columns. So we can compute row = idx / N, col = idx % N. This works if we treat output as row-major (C[row][col]).

Thus:

```
__global__ void matmul_kernel(float* C, const float* A, const float* B, int M, int K, int N) {
    int idx = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (idx >= M * N) return;
    int row = idx / N;
    int col = idx % N;
    float sum = 0.0f;
    for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) {
        // A[k][row] = A[k * M + row]
        // B[k][col] = B[k * N + col]
        sum += A[k * M + row] * B[k * N + col];
    }
    C[idx] = sum;
}
```

This kernel uses each thread computing one output element. Complexity O(M*N*K). With M=2048, N=2048, K=8192 (since K = 4096*2 = 8192). So operations ~ 4M * 8192 ≈ 34B multiply-adds, which might be heavy but okay for a demo.

We can set blockDim.x = 256, numBlocks = (M*N + 255)/256.
